chapters.title: The Community
chapters.description: Jonas lives in a seemingly perfect community with strict rules. He prepares for the Ceremony of Twelve where children receive their life Assignments.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.description: Jonas is selected as the next Receiver of Memory and begins training with the old man who holds all of humanity's memories.

chapters.title: Memories and Truth
chapters.description: Jonas receives increasingly painful memories and learns the dark truth about what 'release' really means in his community.

chapters.title: Escape
chapters.description: Jonas learns Gabriel is scheduled for release and decides to flee the community with the baby, heading toward Elsewhere.

questions.question: What is the name of the main character?
What age is Jonas when he receives his Assignment?
What is 'Sameness' in the community?
options: The elimination of differences, choices, and emotions

questions.question: Who is Gabriel?
options: A baby Jonas's father cares for

questions.question: What genre is The Giver?
The community in The Giver believes they live in a utopia. Is this true?
What happens at the Ceremony of Twelve?
options: Children receive their life Assignments from the Elders

questions.question: How does the community control the weather?
options: They do not — weather is natural
Through climate control that eliminates snow, sunshine variation, and seasons

questions.question: What are 'stirrings' in the community?
options: Romantic or sexual feelings that citizens must suppress with pills

questions.question: What Assignment does Jonas receive?
What is the first memory the Giver transmits to Jonas?
What can Jonas do that others in the community cannot?
What is the main theme of the book?
options: The importance of choice and individuality

questions.question: Why is the Receiver the most important job?
options: The Receiver holds all of humanity's memories and advises the Elders

questions.question: How does the Giver transmit memories to Jonas?
options: By placing his hands on Jonas's bare back

questions.question: What does 'release' actually mean in the community?
What happens when Jonas stops taking his pills?
options: He begins to have feelings and stirrings

questions.question: What does Jonas learn about his father's job?
What happens to people's memories when they are released?
Why was Rosemary released?
options: She asked to be released after receiving painful memories

questions.question: What does Jonas see for the first time in Chapter 12?
Can Jonas give memories to other people by the end of the book?
What does Jonas decide to do at the end of the book?
What does the ending suggest about Jonas and Gabriel's fate?
options: They both die in the snow
It is ambiguous — they may have reached Elsewhere or Jonas may be hallucinating

questions.question: Why does Jonas decide he must flee immediately?
options: The Giver tells him to leave
He learns Gabriel will be released the next morning
He receives a painful memory that scares him

questions.question: How does Jonas protect Gabriel from the search planes during their escape?
options: He transmits memories of calm and nothingness to Gabriel so he does not cry
He wraps Gabriel in a blanket

questions.question: What does the sled and the music Jonas senses at the end of the book represent?
options: The memories returning to the community
Hope and the possibility of a better world

questions.question: What memory of war does the Giver share with Jonas, and why is it important?
options: A memory of a great victory
A painful memory of death and suffering that shows Jonas why Sameness was created
A memory of a peace treaty
A future memory of war coming

writing_prompts.prompt: Jonas's community gave up freedom and emotion for safety and order. Write 150-300 words about whether you think this is a good trade. What would you give up for a peaceful, safe life?
The Giver says memories give life meaning even when they are painful. Write 150-300 words about an important memory — good or bad — that has shaped who you are.
Jonas discovers something terrible that his community hides. Write 150-300 words about the importance of truth. Is it always better to know the truth even if it is painful? Give examples.
The ending of The Giver is ambiguous — we do not know if Jonas and Gabriel survive. Write 150-300 words about what you think happened. Use evidence from the book to support your interpretation.

chapters.title: Maycomb and the Finch Family
chapters.description: Scout Finch introduces Maycomb, Alabama in the 1930s, her father Atticus, brother Jem, and their summer friend Dill. They are fascinated by the reclusive Boo Radley.

chapters.title: Tom Robinson's Trial
chapters.description: Atticus defends Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman, Mayella Ewell. The trial exposes the town's deep racism.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Lessons
chapters.description: Tom is convicted despite being innocent. Bob Ewell seeks revenge against Atticus. Boo Radley saves Scout and Jem from an attack.

chapters.title: Courage and Morality
chapters.description: Scout reflects on the lessons she has learned from Atticus about courage, justice, empathy, and the coexistence of good and evil in people.

questions.question: Who is the narrator of To Kill a Mockingbird?
What is the name of the town where the story takes place?
What is Atticus Finch's job?
Who is Boo Radley?
options: A reclusive neighbor the children are both afraid of and curious about

questions.question: What gifts does Boo Radley leave for Scout and Jem?
options: Small trinkets and gifts hidden in a tree knothole

questions.question: What decade does the story take place in?
What advice does Atticus give Scout about understanding people?
options: You never really understand a person until you climb into their skin and walk around in it

questions.question: What does Miss Maudie tell Scout about mockingbirds?
options: It is a sin to kill them because they only make music and do no harm

questions.question: Who is Calpurnia?
Who is Tom Robinson accused of attacking?
What evidence does Atticus present to show Tom Robinson is innocent?
options: A witness who saw the real attacker
Tom's right arm is disabled, but the attacker was left-handed like Bob Ewell
A written confession from Bob Ewell

questions.question: Despite Atticus's strong defense, what does the jury decide?
Why does the all-white jury convict Tom Robinson even though the evidence shows he is innocent?
options: Racism — in 1930s Alabama they will not take a Black man's word over a white woman's

questions.question: What happens to Tom Robinson after the trial?
options: He is shot and killed trying to escape from prison

questions.question: Why does Atticus agree to defend Tom Robinson?
options: Because he believes every person deserves a fair defense and justice matters regardless of race

questions.question: Who attacks Scout and Jem near the end of the book?
Who saves Scout and Jem from the attack?
What does Scout realize about Boo Radley by the end of the story?
options: He is kind and has been watching over and protecting the children all along

questions.question: What does the title 'To Kill a Mockingbird' mean?
options: It symbolizes the destruction of innocence, as Tom Robinson and Boo Radley are 'mockingbirds'
It is about a bird that causes trouble
It refers to the Finch family name

questions.question: What is the main theme of To Kill a Mockingbird?
options: Racial injustice, moral courage, and the loss of innocence

questions.question: How does Scout change from the beginning to the end of the book?
options: She grows from an innocent child to someone who understands injustice and empathy
She becomes more like her father

questions.question: Who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird?
What does Atticus say is the one place all men are truly equal?
What does Atticus's decision to defend Tom Robinson cost him in the community?
options: He faces hostility, insults, and threats from white townspeople
He is forced to leave Maycomb

questions.question: What is Bob Ewell's motive for accusing Tom Robinson?
options: He wants to cover up his own abuse of Mayella and punish Tom for resisting Mayella's advances
He has a grudge against the Finch family

questions.question: What does Atticus mean when he says he could not hold his head up in town if he did not defend Tom?
options: He has a personal code of ethics that he must live by regardless of public opinion
He is ordered to by the judge
He is afraid of the consequences

questions.question: What does Scout's first-grade teacher, Miss Caroline, do that upsets Scout?
options: She gives Scout a bad grade
She tells Scout her father taught her wrong and she should not read at home

writing_prompts.prompt: Atticus tells Scout to 'climb into someone's skin and walk around in it.' Write 150-300 words about a time you tried to understand someone very different from you. What did you learn?
Tom Robinson is convicted despite being innocent because of racism. Write 150-300 words about a time you saw or experienced injustice. What happened? What should have been done differently?
Boo Radley is feared by the community but he saves the children. Write 150-300 words about a person who is judged unfairly by others. How can we avoid judging people before we know them?
Atticus Finch shows moral courage by defending Tom Robinson even when the whole town is against him. Write 150-300 words about what moral courage means to you and describe someone who shows it.

chapters.title: Celie's Early Life
chapters.description: Celie writes letters to God describing her abuse at the hands of her stepfather and her separation from her sister Nettie after she is married off to Mister.

chapters.title: Shug Avery and Awakening
chapters.description: Mister's lover Shug Avery comes to stay. Celie and Shug form a deep bond that helps Celie discover her own strength, identity, and capacity for love.

chapters.title: Nettie's Letters
chapters.description: Celie discovers that Mister has been hiding letters from her sister Nettie for years. Nettie's letters describe her life in Africa as a missionary.

chapters.title: Freedom and Reunion
chapters.description: Celie leaves Mister, builds an independent life, and is eventually reunited with Nettie. She transforms from a victim into a self-determined woman.

questions.question: What form does The Color Purple take?
Who does Celie address her early letters to?
Who is Nettie to Celie?
options: Her sister whom she loves deeply

questions.question: What does Celie's stepfather do to her?
options: He abuses and rapes her and then marries her off to Mister
He sends her to live with relatives

questions.question: What does Mister (Albert) do to control Celie?
options: He physically abuses her, treats her as a servant, and hides her sister's letters
He sends her back to her family
He locks her in a room

questions.question: Where is Nettie when she writes her letters to Celie?
What is the setting of The Color Purple?
options: Rural Georgia in the early 20th century

questions.question: What is the name of the man Celie is forced to marry?
How does Celie survive her terrible situation early in the book?
options: She endures by staying quiet and escaping into her letters to God

questions.question: Who is Shug Avery?
options: A famous blues singer and Mister's longtime lover

questions.question: How does Shug Avery change Celie's life?
options: She helps Celie discover her worth, find her voice, and see herself as a person deserving of love

questions.question: What does Shug teach Celie about God?
options: God is not a man in church but a force inside everything, including nature
She should stop writing letters to God

questions.question: What does the relationship between Celie and Shug represent in the novel?
options: Female solidarity and love that empowers both women

questions.question: What does Celie discover Mister has been doing with Nettie's letters?
options: Hiding them in a trunk for years without giving them to Celie

questions.question: To whom does Celie address her letters later in the novel?
What happens to Celie's children who were taken from her?
options: They were adopted by Samuel and Nettie as missionaries and grew up in Africa
They were given to an orphanage

questions.question: What business does Celie start to support herself?
How does Mister change by the end of the novel?
options: He shows remorse, becomes kinder, and helps Celie reunite with Nettie

questions.question: What is the main theme of The Color Purple?
options: Resilience, female empowerment, and self-discovery through hardship

questions.question: Who is the author of The Color Purple?
How does the novel end for Celie?
options: Celie reunites with Nettie and her children and lives independently

questions.question: What does the color purple symbolize in the novel?
options: Royalty, beauty, and the joy that God places in the world for people to notice

questions.question: Why does Harpo (Mister's son) struggle in his marriage to Sofia?
options: He tries to control Sofia like his father controls Celie, but Sofia is strong and refuses to be dominated

questions.question: What does Sofia's story add to the novel's themes?
options: A contrast showing a Black woman who fights back against domination, facing severe punishment from white society

questions.question: What does Nettie's experience in Africa show about identity and belonging?
options: It shows that Black Americans have African roots and raises questions about cultural identity
Nettie wants to stay in Africa permanently

questions.question: What does Celie's transformation show about the human spirit?
options: That even after great suffering, a person can find strength, identity, and joy
That revenge is necessary for healing
That moving to a new place solves problems

questions.question: What role does writing letters play for Celie?
options: It is her only outlet for expression and a way to preserve her inner self under oppression

writing_prompts.prompt: Celie survives terrible abuse by staying quiet and writing letters. Write 150-300 words about how writing or another form of expression can help people deal with pain. Give examples from the book and your own life.
Shug Avery helps Celie believe in herself. Write 150-300 words about a person who helped you or someone you know become more confident. What did they say or do? Why did it matter?

Celie and Nettie are separated for many years but never stop loving each other. Write 150-300 words about the importance of family bonds. Can family relationships survive long separations? Use examples.
By the end of the novel Celie is a free, independent woman. Write 150-300 words about what freedom means to you. What does a person need in order to be truly free?

chapters.title: George and Lennie
chapters.description: George Milton and Lennie Small, two migrant workers, travel together in Depression-era California sharing a dream of owning their own farm.

chapters.title: The Ranch
chapters.description: George and Lennie arrive at a ranch to work. They meet the hostile Curley, his flirtatious wife, and lonely ranch hands including Candy and Crooks.

chapters.title: The Dream Collapses
chapters.description: Lennie accidentally kills Curley's wife. George finds Lennie and, to protect him from a violent mob, shoots him himself.

chapters.title: Loneliness and the American Dream
chapters.description: Themes of loneliness, the impossibility of the American Dream, and the friendship between George and Lennie are examined throughout the story.

questions.question: Who are the two main characters in Of Mice and Men?
What is the dream that George and Lennie share?
options: To own their own small farm with rabbits and live off the land
To save enough money to retire

questions.question: What is Lennie's main characteristic?
options: He is physically powerful but mentally disabled and childlike
He is angry and violent by nature

questions.question: What does Lennie love to pet?
options: Soft things like mice, rabbits, and soft hair

questions.question: Why did George and Lennie have to flee their last job?
options: Lennie touched a woman's dress and people thought he attacked her

questions.question: Who is Curley?
options: The boss's aggressive, small son who is hostile to Lennie

questions.question: What does Curley's wife represent in the novel?
options: A lonely woman trapped by her marriage with no other options
A villain who causes trouble on purpose

questions.question: Who is Crooks and what makes his situation special?
options: The foreman who runs the ranch
The only Black worker, who is segregated from the other men and deeply lonely

questions.question: What does Candy offer to contribute to George and Lennie's dream?
options: His savings, making the dream seem briefly possible

questions.question: What happens to Candy's old dog?
options: Carlson shoots it because it is old and suffering

questions.question: How does Curley's wife die?
options: Lennie accidentally breaks her neck while stroking her hair

questions.question: Why does George shoot Lennie at the end?
options: To spare Lennie from a brutal death at the hands of the mob, killing him gently while telling him about their dream

questions.question: What is George telling Lennie just before he dies?
options: He is describing their dream farm so Lennie dies with a happy vision in mind
He is saying goodbye to the ranch
He is reading a letter from family

questions.question: What is the main theme of Of Mice and Men?
options: The loneliness of working men and the fragility of the American Dream

questions.question: Who is the author of Of Mice and Men?
What does Lennie's dream farm represent for all the lonely ranch workers?
options: A real possibility they will achieve
A shared impossible hope that gives temporary purpose to otherwise hopeless lives
A plan they are actively saving for

questions.question: What does the title 'Of Mice and Men' refer to?
options: A line from a Robert Burns poem: 'The best-laid plans of mice and men often go awry'
The small and powerful on the ranch

questions.question: What is the setting of Of Mice and Men?
How does Slim treat George and Lennie differently from Curley?
options: He is the respected, calm foreman who shows understanding and quiet authority without hostility
He reports them to the boss

questions.question: What does Candy's regret about his dog teach about the ending with Lennie?
options: That it is always wrong to kill animals
That it is better to do a hard thing yourself with love than to let someone cruel do it
That old things should be put away
That decisions should be made by groups

questions.question: How does Crooks respond when Lennie visits his room?
options: He is at first hostile and bitter, then opens up because he is desperate for company

questions.question: What does the novella suggest about friendship between men during the Great Depression?
options: Deep friendship was rare and precious, making George and Lennie's bond unusual and meaningful
All ranch workers were close friends
Friendship was only for wealthy men

questions.question: What does Curley's reaction to his wife's death tell us about him?
options: He uses it as an excuse for revenge rather than showing genuine grief for her

questions.question: Why does George need Lennie despite all the trouble Lennie causes?
options: Lennie gives George's life a purpose and companionship, preventing the total loneliness of ranch life
George promised Lennie's aunt he would care for him

questions.question: What happens to Candy's hopes after Curley's wife dies?
options: The dream of the farm dies — he knows it will never happen now
He plans to continue without George and Lennie

questions.question: How does Of Mice and Men portray the American Dream?
options: As always achievable with hard work
As a cruel illusion that is just out of reach for the poor and powerless
As a goal that takes many generations to reach

questions.question: What is Slim's reaction after George shoots Lennie?
options: He shows quiet understanding, telling George he had no choice
He reports George to the police

writing_prompts.prompt: George and Lennie's friendship is unusual — one is clever, one is strong but childlike. Write 150-300 words about what makes a friendship strong even when two people are very different from each other.
Crooks says that a person goes crazy if he has nobody to talk to. Write 150-300 words about the importance of human connection. What happens to people when they are isolated and lonely?

George makes an extremely painful decision at the end of the book to protect Lennie. Write 150-300 words about a time someone made a very difficult choice out of love or loyalty. Was it the right decision?

Of Mice and Men suggests that the American Dream is often out of reach for ordinary people. Write 150-300 words about whether you believe anyone can achieve their dreams with hard work, or whether circumstances make some dreams impossible.

chapters.title: Who Was Chris McCandless?
chapters.description: Jon Krakauer introduces Christopher McCandless, who abandoned his conventional life after college, gave away his savings, and disappeared into the American wilderness.

chapters.title: The Long Journey
chapters.description: McCandless travels through the American West under the name 'Alexander Supertramp,' working briefly and living off the land before heading to Alaska.

chapters.title: Into the Wild
chapters.description: McCandless enters the Alaskan wilderness alone in April 1992 with minimal supplies, living in an abandoned bus and surviving on small game and plants.

chapters.title: Death and Meaning
chapters.description: McCandless dies alone in the bus in August 1992, likely from starvation. Krakauer explores what his story means and reflects on his own youthful adventures.

questions.question: What does Christopher McCandless do with his savings after graduating from college?
options: He donates the approximately $24,000 to charity and gives away his possessions
He uses it to travel to Europe
He gives it to his parents

questions.question: What alias does McCandless use during his travels?
What is McCandless's relationship with his parents like?
options: Conflicted — he is angry at their materialism and his father's hidden past

questions.question: Who is the author of Into the Wild?
What kind of book is Into the Wild?
What writers most influenced McCandless's philosophy?
What did McCandless discover about his father that angered him deeply?
options: His father was not his real father
His father had a secret second family and had lied about it for years

questions.question: What job does McCandless take in the American West during his journey?
options: He works at a grain elevator in South Dakota for a time

questions.question: What does McCandless's treatment of people he meets along the way show?
options: He forms genuine and warm connections with many people despite his desire for solitude
He only talks to people when he needs something

questions.question: Who is Wayne Westerberg and what is his relationship with McCandless?
options: A police officer who arrests McCandless
A South Dakota farmer who befriends McCandless and gives him work

questions.question: What does McCandless call the abandoned bus where he lives in Alaska?
Why is McCandless unable to leave the Alaskan wilderness when he wants to?
options: The Teklanika River has risen with snowmelt and is too dangerous to cross

questions.question: What likely causes McCandless's death?
options: Starvation, possibly worsened by accidentally eating toxic seeds

questions.question: What does McCandless write in his journal near the end of his life?
options: He writes 'HAPPINESS ONLY REAL WHEN SHARED' suggesting he has changed his views on solitude

questions.question: What is Krakauer's main argument about McCandless?
options: McCandless was simply foolish and reckless
McCandless was idealistic and brave, even if his preparation was poor — his journey had real meaning

questions.question: What does Krakauer share about his own life to connect with McCandless's story?
options: His own youthful attempt to solo-climb a dangerous Alaskan peak called the Devil's Thumb
His experience as a park ranger

questions.question: What is the main theme of Into the Wild?
options: The search for authentic meaning outside society, and the tension between idealism and reality

questions.question: How does McCandless feel about material possessions and money?
options: He sees them as obstacles to a true and meaningful life
He wants to earn as much money as possible

questions.question: What does McCandless's willingness to form friendships with elderly and working-class people suggest?
options: He values authentic human connection more than social status
He is looking for parental figures
He avoids people his own age

questions.question: What basic survival mistake does McCandless make when preparing for Alaska?
options: He brings very inadequate supplies — no map, wrong rifle, too little food — underestimating the wilderness
He does not bring a tent

questions.question: What does McCandless's story say about the gap between romantic ideals and reality?
options: High ideals without practical preparation can lead to tragedy
Reality is always better than ideals
Ideals are foolish and should be abandoned

questions.question: What happens to McCandless's family after his death?
options: They are devastated, especially his sister Carine, and struggle to understand his choices
They support the idea that he died doing what he loved

questions.question: What does McCandless's journey along the Colorado River in a canoe show about him?
options: He is adventurous and resourceful but also lucky — he nearly drowns and gets lost
He is trying to reach Mexico

questions.question: What does McCandless shoot and eat to survive in Alaska?
options: Moose and small game including squirrels, birds, and porcupines
Canned food he found in the bus

questions.question: How did hikers discover McCandless's body?
options: A group of hunters found the bus and his decomposed body inside his sleeping bag
He was found by a park ranger

questions.question: What does McCandless's graduation gift car represent in the story?
options: A connection to his family and old life that he eventually abandons in a flash flood

questions.question: What does the elderly man Ron Franz do for McCandless and what does McCandless do that breaks his heart?
options: He gives McCandless money but McCandless steals more
He deeply bonds with McCandless and offers to adopt him, but McCandless leaves and then dies before they can meet again
He teaches McCandless to hike and McCandless never contacts him
He warns McCandless not to go to Alaska and McCandless ignores him

questions.question: What does Krakauer compare McCandless to in order to show his journey is not unique?
options: Famous explorers like Lewis and Clark
Other young men throughout history who have left society for wilderness and risk

writing_prompts.prompt: McCandless gave away all his money and walked away from his comfortable life. Write 200-400 words about what you think motivated him. Do you admire his choice or think it was foolish? Explain with reasons.

McCandless wrote 'Happiness only real when shared.' Do you agree? Write 200-400 words about whether true happiness requires other people or if a person can find it alone. Use examples from the book and your own life.
McCandless was idealistic but underprepared. Write 200-400 words about the balance between following your dreams and being realistic and prepared. When does idealism become dangerous?
Krakauer shares his own risky adventure to help readers understand McCandless. Write 200-400 words about a risk you have taken or would like to take. What drives people to seek danger and challenge?

chapters.title: Nick Arrives in West Egg
chapters.description: Nick Carraway moves to West Egg, Long Island, next door to the mysterious Jay Gatsby. He visits his cousin Daisy Buchanan and her husband Tom across the bay in East Egg.

chapters.title: Gatsby's World
chapters.description: Nick attends one of Gatsby's lavish parties and finally meets him. He learns Gatsby is in love with Daisy, whom he knew five years ago, and is reunited with her.

chapters.title: The Dream Unravels
chapters.description: The truth about Gatsby's past is revealed. Tom confronts Gatsby. Daisy kills Myrtle in a car accident. Gatsby is shot dead. Nick reflects on the emptiness of Gatsby's dream.

chapters.title: The American Dream and Its Illusions
chapters.description: Nick organizes Gatsby's funeral — almost no one attends. He returns to the Midwest, disillusioned with the East and its shallow, careless wealth.

questions.question: Who is the narrator of The Great Gatsby?
Where does Nick live in relation to Gatsby?
options: He is Gatsby's next-door neighbor in West Egg
He lives in East Egg with the Buchanans
He lives in New York City

questions.question: How does Gatsby make his money?
options: He inherited it from his parents
He made it through illegal bootlegging and organized crime

questions.question: What is the difference between East Egg and West Egg?
options: East Egg represents old money and established families; West Egg represents new, self-made wealth

questions.question: What does the green light at the end of Daisy's dock symbolize?
options: Gatsby's dream and longing for Daisy and what she represents — an ideal that is always just out of reach
The color of hope in general

questions.question: What is Tom Buchanan's character like?
options: Arrogant, racist, unfaithful, and careless with people's lives

questions.question: What does Jordan Baker do for a living?
options: She is a socialite with no job

questions.question: What decade does The Great Gatsby take place in?
What is Gatsby's goal in holding his lavish parties?
options: He hopes Daisy will one day wander in, and it is a way to show off his wealth to win her back
He is trying to become famous
He wants to make business connections

questions.question: What does Gatsby ask Nick to do for him?
options: Arrange a reunion with Daisy at Nick's house
Help him move to New York

questions.question: What does Gatsby want from Daisy when they reunite?
options: He wants to be friends again
He wants her to say she never loved Tom and repeat the past with him
He wants her to meet his parents

questions.question: What is Tom Buchanan's affair and with whom?
options: He is secretly seeing Jordan Baker
He is having an affair with Myrtle Wilson, a mechanic's wife in the Valley of Ashes
He has no affair — it is a rumor
He is seeing one of Gatsby's party guests

questions.question: Who is driving Gatsby's car when Myrtle Wilson is killed?
Who shoots Gatsby and why?
options: George Wilson, Myrtle's husband, who believes Gatsby killed his wife

questions.question: How does Daisy respond to Gatsby's death?
options: She is devastated and attends the funeral
She leaves with Tom without attending the funeral or even contacting Nick
She confesses everything to the police

questions.question: Who attends Gatsby's funeral?
options: Almost no one — his father, a few servants, and Nick
The people from the Valley of Ashes

questions.question: What does the Valley of Ashes represent?
options: The moral and social decay hidden beneath the glittering surface of the wealthy class

questions.question: What is the main theme of The Great Gatsby?
options: The corruption and hollowness of the American Dream in the 1920s

questions.question: Who is the author of The Great Gatsby?
What does Nick mean when he calls Tom and Daisy 'careless people'?
options: They smash up things and creatures and then retreat into their money, leaving others to clean up their mess

questions.question: What does Gatsby's confrontation with Tom at the Plaza Hotel reveal?
options: That Gatsby is richer than Tom
That Daisy's love cannot withstand Tom's class privilege — she will not leave him for Gatsby
That Tom is afraid of Gatsby
That Nick dislikes both men equally

questions.question: What are 'the eyes of Doctor T.J. Eckleburg' and what do they symbolize?
options: A real optometrist's advertisement that symbolizes the eyes of God watching a morally empty society
A character who watches the other characters

questions.question: What does Nick's narration suggest about his own character?
options: He claims to be one of the few honest people he knows, though he is not entirely objective
He is in love with Daisy
He disapproves of everyone he meets

questions.question: What does Gatsby's shirt-throwing scene with Daisy reveal about their relationship?
options: It shows that Daisy's love for Gatsby is partly about his wealth and what it represents

questions.question: What does Nick realize about the East by the end of the novel?
options: It is better than the Midwest
It represents moral corruption, carelessness, and the emptiness of wealth — he returns to the Midwest
It is a place of opportunity
He wants to return there someday

questions.question: What does the famous last line of the novel mean: 'So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past'?
options: Humans constantly strive forward but are always pulled back by the past and cannot escape it
The American Dream is always ahead of us

questions.question: What was Gatsby's real name before he reinvented himself?

writing_prompts.prompt: Gatsby reinvented himself completely to pursue his dream. Write 200-400 words about whether it is possible or desirable to completely reinvent yourself. What would you change about yourself and why?
Gatsby throws lavish parties but is ultimately alone. Write 200-400 words about the difference between popularity and true friendship. Can wealth buy genuine connection with other people?
Tom and Daisy are described as 'careless people.' Write 200-400 words about the responsibility that comes with wealth and power. What obligations do privileged people have toward others?

The American Dream in The Great Gatsby is shown to be hollow and corrupt. Write 200-400 words about what the American Dream means today. Is it still a valid concept, or has it been distorted by materialism?
